ai.description: Pruthi's skink reaches a snout-vent length of 4–5 cm. It is brown with a dark lateral stripe and possesses a translucent lower eyelid. It is distinguished by its pentadactyl limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dravidoseps pruthi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark dorsolateral stripe that extends from the snout through the eye, contrasting with its pale flanks.
ai.habitat: Pruthi’s skink inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Pruthi's skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmer daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: Dravidoseps pruthi is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Dravidoseps pruthi is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in India, specifically inhabiting high-elevation grasslands and forests in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
